mcqs.question: What is the Council of Ministers in the Indian parliamentary system?

options.A: A body of elected representatives that assists the President in ceremonial duties.
options.B: A group of senior civil servants who permanently run the ministries.
options.C: A collective of ministers, headed by the Prime Minister, responsible for running the government and advising the President.
options.D: A committee of judges that reviews legislative bills.

mcqs.answer: A collective of ministers, headed by the Prime Minister, responsible for running the government and advising the President.
mcqs.explanation: The Council of Ministers is the group of ministers, led by the Prime Minister, that formulates and implements government policies and advises the President. It is not a ceremonial body, nor is it made up of permanent civil servants or judges.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly matches the type of executive with its description in India?

options.A: Political executive – the President and Prime Minister; Permanent executive – the Union Public Service Commission.
options.B: Political executive – the Council of Ministers; Permanent executive – the civil services (IAS, IPS) that remain in office irrespective of changes in government.
options.C: Political executive – the Supreme Court; Permanent executive – the Election Commission.
options.D: Political executive – the State Legislative Assemblies; Permanent executive – the Governors.

mcqs.answer: Political executive – the Council of Ministers; Permanent executive – the civil services (IAS, IPS) that remain in office irrespective of changes in government.
mcqs.explanation: The political executive consists of elected officials such as the President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, whose tenure depends on electoral outcomes. The permanent executive comprises career civil servants who stay in their posts regardless of which party forms the government. Options A, C and D mix up institutions and their roles.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand collective responsibility at a basic level
mcqs.question: If the Council of Ministers decides to increase the tax on luxury goods, and the government later faces criticism for the decision, who is held accountable in the parliamentary system?

options.C: All members of the Council of Ministers collectively.

mcqs.answer: All members of the Council of Ministers collectively.
mcqs.explanation: Collective responsibility means that the entire Council of Ministers is answerable to the Parliament for its decisions. If a policy is unpopular, the whole cabinet may be required to resign, not just the minister who introduced it. The President does not bear political responsibility for such decisions.

mcqs.question: During a constitutional crisis, the President receives a report that the Prime Minister has lost the confidence of the Lok Sabha but refuses to resign. What constitutional power can the President exercise in this situation?

options.A: Dismiss the Prime Minister and appoint a new one who can command majority.
options.B: Unilaterally pass a law to remove the Prime Minister.
options.D: Issue an advisory opinion without any effect.

mcqs.answer: Dismiss the Prime Minister and appoint a new one who can command majority.
mcqs.explanation: If a Prime Minister loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha, the President can ask for a floor test and, if the loss is confirmed, dismiss the Prime Minister and invite another leader who enjoys majority support. The President cannot legislate unilaterally, nor can he/she merely issue an advisory opinion.

mcqs.question: The Prime Minister can remain in office even if his/her party loses the majority in the Lok Sabha, as long as the President approves. Which statement is false?

options.A: The Prime Minister must resign if he/she loses majority support.
options.B: The President can ask the Prime Minister to prove majority.
options.C: The Prime Minister can continue without majority until elections.
options.D: The Prime Minister is appointed by the President but must have majority support.

mcqs.answer: The Prime Minister can continue without majority until elections.
mcqs.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the Prime Minister must enjoy the confidence of the Lok Sabha. If the majority is lost, the Prime Minister is expected to resign or seek a confidence vote. The President cannot simply allow the PM to stay without majority. Options A, B and D correctly describe the constitutional requirement.

mcqs.question: Why is the principle of collective responsibility important for the Council of Ministers in India?

options.A: It ensures that each minister can act independently without consulting others.
options.B: It allows the government to present a united front and be held accountable as a whole for its policies.
options.C: It gives the President the power to dismiss individual ministers at will.
options.D: It separates the legislative and executive functions completely.

mcqs.answer: It allows the government to present a united front and be held accountable as a whole for its policies.
mcqs.explanation: Collective responsibility means that all ministers share the same stance on policies and are jointly answerable to Parliament. This unity ensures stability and clear accountability. Option A describes the opposite of collective responsibility, while C and D are unrelated to the principle.

mcqs.question: Which statement best compares the political executive with the permanent executive in India?

options.A: The political executive (President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers) changes with elections, whereas the permanent executive (civil servants) remains in service irrespective of political changes.
options.B: Both the political and permanent executives are appointed by the President for fixed ten-year terms.
options.C: The permanent executive makes policy decisions, while the political executive implements them.
options.D: The political executive consists only of the judiciary, while the permanent executive includes the legislature.

mcqs.answer: The political executive (President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers) changes with elections, whereas the permanent executive (civil servants) remains in service irrespective of political changes.
mcqs.explanation: The political executive is made up of elected officials whose tenure depends on electoral outcomes. The permanent executive comprises career civil servants (IAS, IPS, etc.) who continue their service regardless of which party forms the government. Options B, C and D misrepresent the nature and functions of these bodies.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand collective responsibility at a basic level
mcqs.question: In the context of the Indian parliamentary system, which of the following statements about collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers is most accurate?

options.A: Only the Prime Minister is answerable to the Parliament for the actions of the Council.
options.B: Each minister is individually responsible for his/her ministry, and the Council as a whole is not answerable.
options.C: The Council of Ministers as a whole must resign if it loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha, reflecting collective responsibility.
options.D: The President can dismiss the Council of Ministers without consulting the Parliament.

mcqs.answer: The Council of Ministers as a whole must resign if it loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha, reflecting collective responsibility.
mcqs.explanation: Collective responsibility means that the entire Council stands or falls together. If the Lok Sabha expresses no confidence, the whole Council must resign. Option A limits responsibility to the Prime Minister, B ignores the collective aspect, and D misstates the President's constitutional powers.
